target_customer: Mid-size employers in Texas (about 51 to 2,000 employees) buying fully insured group health plans
problem: Mid-size employers face expensive health insurance and weak care; Evry sold plans it said cost 20% less with no deductibles or copays.
business_model: Licensed health insurer selling fully insured group plans via brokers

founders.name: Chris Gay
founders.background_notes: Per YC bio also led a P&C insurance software stack (2012) and a turnaround of an IP and services company (2016).

technical_complexity.rationale: Insurance software and claims automation are standard engineering, but standing up a licensed carrier adds regulatory and actuarial work.

defensibility.rationale: A state insurance license and actuarial pricing are barriers, but product design is copyable.

incumbents: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Texas
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Globe Life bought Evry in October 2023 and kept it as a subsidiary.

market_need_then: Employer health costs were rising and mid-size employers lacked access to wellness plans common at large employers, per launch coverage in 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: No coverage of the brand itself; the name is a variant of 'every' with some confusion risk with unrelated companies named Evry or Everis.

outcome_analysis: Evry spent about four years building a licensed carrier, launched publicly in Dallas in November 2021, and sold to Globe Life in October 2023 on undisclosed terms. It continues as a Globe Life subsidiary. The regulatory position and an insurer buyer seeking group health growth explain the exit, but the price and traction are not public.
notes: Funding figures are aggregator only, unverified: CB Insights $7.44M over five rounds, seedtable seed of about $7.6M in 2021-07; no Series B found. The BusinessWire launch release returned 403 so no round was confirmed from a primary source; Form D (CIK 0001870261) not opened. No competitor sources dated near 2018 found. Company site now describes it as a Globe Life company.
